entries.title: Shap — The Scheduling Asterisk
entries.teaser: The Almanac preserves Shap's post-expansion playoff drought and the 2015 scheduling error.
body: The 2015 standings note a scheduling error: Shap finished last, and the incorrectly assigned Saunders opener changed the counterfactual path. The alternate result is labeled rather than rewriting the canonical table.
The Almanac also records Shap's later playoff drought, deferred 2020 VPC election, and tension between house rules and the casino. These are reviewed narrative details; records remain canonical JSON.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 3–5; counterfactuals are labeled and numbers remain canonical.

entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 10–11; narrative only.

entries.title: Nuss — Dizzy Bat Relay
entries.teaser: A 2018 relay collision became one of the Almanac's unforgettable draft-weekend moments.
body: During the 2018 relay, Nuss slammed his head into a tree during dizzy bat and still had three spins to go. The Almanac preserves the anecdote as draft-weekend lore without diagnosing an injury or changing canonical results.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed page 10; narrative only.

entries.title: Plot — The Joel Asterisks
entries.teaser: The 2020–21 Plot/Joel disputes are preserved as attributed league lore.
body: The Almanac notes that Plotnick was the only person kicked out of the J during Knarr's tenure, then describes Plotnick's 2020 final, a manually changed playoff format, and three later one-sided trades. These are attributed league-history claims and alternate-format context, not findings about real people or a rewrite of standings.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 13–14; attributed fantasy-league lore.

entries.title: Plot — The VPC-Origin Trade
entries.teaser: A Plot/Zook trade helped inspire the VPC role.
body: The Almanac connects a Demarco Murray/Todd Gurley trade between Plotnick and Zook with the later VPC role. It is retained as league administration history and does not change the canonical transaction ledger.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed page 14; narrative context only.

entries.title: Connor Maio — Bye the Time
entries.teaser: Connor's Almanac section follows early success, repeated Saunders trips, and the LeVeon Bell decision.
body: The Almanac describes Connor's immediate 2015 success after expansion, two Saunders championships, the LeVeon Bell decision, and repeated returns to the Saunders final. The punishment risk and collapse language remain fantasy-league narrative, not probability claims.
The profile records Connor's resilience and rivalry context through the 2024 material. Current standings, finishes, and game scores remain canonical JSON facts.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 17–21; numbers remain canonical assets.

entries.title: Connor — LeVeon Bell
entries.teaser: Connor's first-round LeVeon Bell pick is part of the 2018 story.
body: The Almanac records LeVeon Bell as Connor's first-round pick in 2018 and notes that Bell did not play a game that season. This is a league-history detail, not a counterfactual bracket or a replacement for canonical results.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 19–21; factual narrative detail only.

entries.title: Connor — The Saunders Run
entries.teaser: Connor's repeated Saunders appearances and punishment risk are documented without invented dates.
body: The Almanac traces Connor's repeated Saunders appearances, including early success and later finals, and the punishment risk attached to that run. Where a specific fantasy season or completion date is not unambiguous, the entry leaves it null and keeps only the reviewed narrative.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 17–21; season mapping remains nullable.

entries.title: Zubs — The Three-Year Peak
entries.teaser: Injuries, the 2018 points record, and the Mahomes era frame Zubs's rise.
body: The Almanac follows Zubs from the 2017 injury-hit season through the 2018 points explosion and three straight ten-win seasons. It then describes the Mahomes-era strategy, playoff breakthroughs, and the later return to the middle of the standings.
The 2022 update also records Zubs's sustained advantage over Plotnick. Scores, records, and titles remain canonical data.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 14–17 (including the 2022 update); numbers remain canonical.

entries.title: Zook — The No-Try Draft
entries.teaser: Zook's admission about 2014 and later draft absences is part of the draft-room record.
body: The Almanac says Zook admitted he did not try in 2014, then follows his dominant 2015–18 stretch and the decline after missing in-person drafts. The story is a draft-weekend anecdote, not a modification to draft slots or season results.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 24–27; narrative only.

entries.title: Haynes — Eight Owners and Expansion
entries.teaser: The original commissioner chose to continue with eight owners and guided SEC expansion.
body: The Almanac credits Haynes with continuing the league in 2014 with eight owners, overseeing expansion to ten teams, and developing the VPC position. It describes the term as controversy-free while leaving all commissioner boundaries shared as supplied.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 33–34; narrative context through 2024.

entries.title: Joel — Commissioner Asterisks
entries.teaser: Joel's commissioner years include attributed collusion lore and a title-era rule dispute.
body: The Almanac describes Joel's election, later collusion accusations and investigations, and the fact that he was not found guilty. It also records the 2020 rule/title context and the 2021 repeat attempt as attributed fantasy-league lore, not factual allegations outside the league.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 30–31; attributed fantasy-league lore.

entries.title: Rishi — Keys, Vive, and Beer Pong
entries.teaser: Rishi Football, the Vive sponsor, and the 2021 draft-weekend win form a distinct Almanac story.
body: The Almanac explains that Rishi Football was an intentional Johnny Manziel reference, records Vive as an unofficial sponsor, and follows the first five playoff exits before the 2021 breakthrough. It also records the eight-hour IHOP challenge and the 2021 draft-weekend beer-pong win with Haynes.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 23–24; narrative only; numbers remain canonical.

entries.title: Haynes — Top Seeds and Collapses

entries.title: Aaron Shapiro — Respect the House
entries.teaser: Shap's Almanac profile spans the house, the casino, and a remarkably complete history.
body: The 2024 Almanac presents Shap as a steady early-era contender: a 2014 finalist, a 2015 Saunders survivor, and a manager whose weekly highs and lows were often more dramatic than his final record.

It records the 2015 scheduling error and the counterfactual Saunders path, the 2018 decision to pass on the first overall pick, and Shap's later VPC service. The profile also reviews his playoff returns and head-to-head balance; records, scores, and finishes remain canonical.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 3–5 (including 2015/2018 notes); numbers remain canonical.

entries.title: Matt Singer — The Lawn and the Relay
entries.teaser: Singer's Almanac profile mixes draft-room lore with a dominant run.
body: The Almanac records Singer's lawn-drinking explanation for missing the inaugural draft, then follows the return, the 2016 title, and the 2017 relay-era personality. It treats the lawn story as draft-weekend lore, not a punishment.
The profile follows the dominant early run, VPC work, mind games, the 2020 format dispute, and later playoff turns. These are 2024 narrative context; outcomes come from canonical data.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 5–8 (including the 2020 update); numbers remain canonical.

entries.title: Dillon Nussbaum — The Mic
entries.teaser: Nuss's profile is a long arc of records, rivalry, and stand-up punishment.
body: The Almanac follows Nuss from an early Saunders appearance through a sustained playoff presence, a close 2020 season, and a canonical low-score record. His rivalry with Rishi, the finger injury, and repeated strategic choices are part of the league's running history.

The profile closes on Nuss fulfilling the virtual stand-up punishment and separating anecdote from measured result. The 2020 near-tie and later playoff drought remain searchable context without replacing canonical tables.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 8–11 (including the 2020 update); numbers remain canonical.

entries.title: Ian Plotnick — The Breakthrough
entries.teaser: Plot's profile tracks the long route to a first playoff breakthrough.
body: The Almanac describes Plotnick's early near-misses, the 2018 playoff breakthrough, four consecutive Saunders wins, and the rivalries and trades that shaped the middle years. It gives the league a narrative record of persistence rather than a new statistical source.

The Demarco Murray/Todd Gurley trade, the 2020 playoff-administration dispute, the 2021 collapse, and Plotnick's 2024 Saunders return remain reviewed context. Scores, standings, slots, and titles come from canonical assets.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 11–14 (through the 2024 section); numbers remain canonical.

entries.title: Zach Brown — The Breakthrough
entries.teaser: Zubs's Almanac profile follows the climb from average seasons to two championships.
body: The Almanac presents Zubs as a balanced owner whose 2018 points explosion and 2019 championship ended a long stretch of near-misses. It follows the injury-hit 2017 season, the three-season regular-season peak, and the strategy of riding one team across years.
The 2022 update covers the return to the middle of the pack, the Saunders win over Plotnick, and the longest-running head-to-head streak. The 2024 margin and all other scores remain canonical facts.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 14–17 (including the 2022 update); numbers remain canonical.

entries.title: Rishi Patel — The Keys
entries.teaser: Rishi's profile is built around hidden keys, rivalries, and a late breakthrough.
body: The Almanac frames Rishi's career through the hidden-keys motif, the long rivalry with Shap, the 2021 turnaround, and the restoration of dignity to the Saunders position through an in-person punishment. It also records his place in the most lopsided rivalry described by the edition.

The 2022 update follows the first playoff win, the eight-hour IHOP challenge, the 2021 beer-pong win, and the 2024 final. This is reviewed league context; records, points, finishes, and margins remain canonical.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 21–24 (including the 2022 update); numbers remain canonical.

entries.title: Michael Zuckerman — The Mahomes Era
entries.teaser: Zook's Almanac profile covers balance, titles, and a run of bold management choices.
body: The Almanac presents Zook as a balanced opponent with a 2018 points explosion, several playoff successes, and a strategy of riding a single team across multiple seasons. It also recounts draft-competition dominance and the management decisions that ended later playoff runs.

The 2022 update contrasts the Mahomes-era titles with the absence-related downturn, the benching decisions that ended the 2021 playoff run, and the continued draft-competition threat. The profile is intentionally narrative; champion, Saunders, record, points, and finishes remain canonical assets.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 24–27 (including the 2022 update); numbers remain canonical assets.

entries.title: Joel Denicoff — Often Imitated
entries.teaser: Joel's profile covers the elevator ride, title defenses, and commissioner years.
body: The Almanac follows Joel from the early championship years through an improbable worst-to-first turn and the head-to-head records that made his two postseason runs distinctive. It preserves the supplied imitation line as personality, not as a claim about copied work.

The 2022 update covers the 2019 near-record season, the COVID-year title, a defending-champion return to the final, and the 2021 election. Commissioner service is a transition-era role; the administrative summary remains separate from season statistics.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 27–31 (including the 2022 update); numbers remain canonical.

entries.title: Joe Haynes — The Original Commissioner
entries.teaser: Joe's profile closes the Almanac with early titles and the first administration.
body: The Almanac describes Haynes as the initial commissioner, organizer of the early league, and a two-time top-seed owner whose title and Saunders runs anchor the opening years. It also notes the 2015 punishment precedent, the 2021 title run, and the later return to strong form.

The 2022 update follows the 2021 collapse-and-rebound and the separate 2021 and 2023 championships before closing on Haynes's expansion and VPC stewardship. This reviewed narrative keeps standings, records, and finishes in canonical season and game data.
entries.provenance: Darling 2024 Almanac, reviewed pages 31–34 (including the 2022 update); numbers remain canonical.
